# AI System Checklist {#sec-ai-checklist}

Use this checklist when a system includes a model, an AI service or an automated recommendation. It is not a certification. It is a set of questions that should have owners and evidence.

## Problem and authority

- [ ] The task the model supports is named.
- [ ] The decision a human owns is named.
- [ ] The consequence of a wrong answer is understood.
- [ ] The system can refuse, escalate or fall back.
- [ ] A human can override the model without fighting the interface.

## Data

- [ ] Every data source has an owner.
- [ ] The freshness requirement is stated.
- [ ] Personal and sensitive data are identified.
- [ ] Data use is permitted by policy and contract.
- [ ] Retrieval sources are versioned or dated.
- [ ] Stale or missing data has a defined behaviour.

## Model and provider

- [ ] The model version is recorded.
- [ ] The provider's change and notice policy is known.
- [ ] The cost per request and monthly cap are known.
- [ ] Latency and availability expectations are recorded.
- [ ] The exit path if the provider changes terms or price is defined.

## Evaluation

- [ ] A held-out evaluation set exists.
- [ ] The metric and threshold are defined.
- [ ] Important slices are evaluated separately.
- [ ] Refusal and unsafe cases are included.
- [ ] The evaluation can be reproduced.
- [ ] The review owner and frequency are named.

## Human oversight

- [ ] The reviewer sees the evidence behind a recommendation.
- [ ] The reviewer has time and authority to disagree.
- [ ] Overrides are logged.
- [ ] Automation bias is discussed with users.
- [ ] Responsibility for the final decision is explicit.

## Security and privacy

- [ ] Prompts do not leak unnecessary personal data.
- [ ] Access control applies to retrieval and logs.
- [ ] Interactions are logged with the right retention.
- [ ] Prompt injection and untrusted content are considered.
- [ ] Incident response covers harmful or misleading output.

## Monitoring and handover

- [ ] Accuracy, refusal, override and incident metrics are monitored.
- [ ] Each metric has a threshold, owner and action.
- [ ] The fallback is tested.
- [ ] The runbook covers model outage and wrong answers.
- [ ] The post-launch review measures the outcome, not usage.
- [ ] The system has an owner after handover.
